   - Additional checks were added after memory allocations to ensure that if the allocation fails, the function returns early to prevent further operations on a NULL pointer.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modifications are related to memory management within the `regmap_debugfs_init` function. The changes ensure that the `debugfs_name` is only allocated when it has not been previously set, thus preventing a memory leak that could occur if the function was called multiple times without freeing the previously allocated memory.
- The fix addresses a specific bug identified in the commit referenced (`Fixes: 9b947a13e7f6`), which introduced the issue of unnecessary memory allocation and potential leaks when attaching devices to the regmap. The new checks and logic ensure that the memory is managed correctly, maintaining the integrity of the system's memory usage.

Fixes: 9b947a13e7f6 ("regmap: use debugfs even when no device")
Signed-off-by: Xiaolei Wang <xiaolei.wang@windriver.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20201229105046.41984-1-xiaolei.wang@windriver.com

        Patch:
        diff --git a/drivers/base/regmap/regmap-debugfs.c b/drivers/base/regmap/regmap-debugfs.c
index 8dfac7f3ed7a..bf03cd343be2 100644
--- a/drivers/base/regmap/regmap-debugfs.c
+++ b/drivers/base/regmap/regmap-debugfs.c
@@ -582,18 +582,25 @@ void regmap_debugfs_init(struct regmap *map)
 		devname = dev_name(map->dev);
 
 	if (name) {
-		map->debugfs_name = kasprintf(GFP_KERNEL, "%s-%s",
+		if (!map->debugfs_name) {
+			map->debugfs_name = kasprintf(GFP_KERNEL, "%s-%s",
 					      devname, name);
+			if (!map->debugfs_name)
+				return;
+		}
 		name = map->debugfs_name;
 	} else {
 		name = devname;
 	}
 
 	if (!strcmp(name, "dummy")) {
-		kfree(map->debugfs_name);
+		if (!map->debugfs_name)
+			kfree(map->debugfs_name);
 
 		map->debugfs_name = kasprintf(GFP_KERNEL, "dummy%d",
 						dummy_index);
+		if (!map->debugfs_name)
+				return;
 		name = map->debugfs_name;
 		dummy_index++;
 	}
